thread:
kai: Hey team, new hire here. M1 Macbook (company) finished OOBE but trying to open some apps and getting Gatekeeper 'unidentified developer' blocks. Also Rosetta installer didn't run automatically. Kandji shows 'Enrolled' but I can't brew install or run docker installer (permission denied). Anyone seen this combo?

renata-it: welcome @kai! quick checks: did you accept the management profile prompt during first login? run `profiles status` and paste output. Also what's the serial?

kai: profiles status: "MDM: Kandji (managed)". serial: C02M1EXAMPLE

it-bot: Ticket RH-9999 created and assigned to renata-it. https://internal.redwood/support/RH-9999

renata-it: ok MDM is present. Gatekeeper/Notarization blocks often happen if post-enroll scripts that install our notarized helper weren't executed. can you try running `sudo /usr/local/bin/redwood-post-enroll` and paste output? I don't have sudo on your machine so ping devex if you need admin.

kai: tried that but permission denied when calling `sudo` — says current user not in sudoers.

devex-lee: I can issue a one-time admin window. please file the devex form: https://internal.redwood/devex/admin-request and paste id here. Note we prefer to push a signed package via MDM instead of handing out sudo.

kai: submitted ADM-9999

devex-lee: approved for 30 minutes. running remote check now; renata, can you trigger the post-enroll script from console for Kai?

renata-it: initiating post-enroll run... output: "Installing notarized helper: success; Rosetta: installing... prompt will appear"

kai: Rosetta prompt popped up, installed. Gatekeeper still blocking Docker.app and Homebrew install errors persist with permission denied for /usr/local.

renata-it: after post-enroll we should fix ownership on /usr/local: run `sudo chown -R $(whoami):admin /usr/local` then retry. Kai, now that you have sudo window, try that.

kai: ran chown command, homebrew installed fine. Docker installer still warns about 'unapproved developer' for a kernel extension and asks to allow in System Settings > Privacy & Security. That requires admin confirmation.

security-sam: kernel extension approval is sensitive. If the kext is from our signed vendor (com.docker.driver), we can push an MDM profile that pre-approves it, but that takes ~10-15min. Alternatively devex can allow manually for this session. Which do you prefer?

devex-lee: prefer MDM push, renata can queue it. Kai we can keep your admin window open until it's resolved; we'll revoke early if not used.

renata-it: pushed kext approval profile. Kai, go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Allow for "Docker, Inc." then restart.

kai: clicked Allow, restarted. Docker installer completed, ran a sample container. FileVault had asked during initial login and is enabled. Everything looks green. Thanks y'all :raised_hands:

it-bot: RH-9999 marked resolved by renata-it.
